qualification_history: A first shell wrapper stopped before Go launch because its secret files intentionally lacked trailing newlines; no candidate or project ran.
The governed package initially lacked the existing built-in probe-helper dispatch; the native probe failed closed and no project ran.
A denial sentinel placed beside the prepared snapshot was correctly reported as fallback-detected; moving it to the already-qualified external source boundary closed the harness error.
A freshly registered agent required AIP signatures, while the frozen MVP is unsigned. The disposable agent now explicitly sets signing_required=false and must pass Core auth before launch.

The first real 409 exposed an invalid exact-two-record assumption: the pinned SDK emits a bounded lifecycle. The adapter now retains every forwarded SDK record and requires exactly one candidate-bound BLOCK.
A later real block exposed missing PA_PORT variables in the test-owned teardown command. The final proof exported the four non-secret ports, and test-owned cleanup passed.
